task_cases.finding: All 30 runs got the direction right; the evaluator only accepts an exact copy of the reference sentence
Reference 2.68 comes from re-calling the untrimmed subsample FASTQs; every run correctly measured the supplied VCF (2.56)
One of the two "3"s came after reading the BixBench key; the reference depends on clusterProfiler defaults the prompt never states
The only accepted runs copied the row filter from downloaded benchmark sources; the reference rests on an asymmetric row filter
The reference uses a retired PhyKIT RCV definition; every Galaxy run computed the current definition correctly
The Galaxy advantage comes from a 2–3-gene difference in foreground size, and the evaluator scores the same answer differently by harness
CCND1 vs CDKN1A is a sign-convention split (raw gene effect vs −gene effect), plus two ranking/indexing bugs
Galaxy's 15/15 comes from the raw-Ct route; code runs that followed the source paper got 1:0
The count depends on whether the gene lists also require padj; DeepSeek's lfc-only lists give 2
Every wrong U traces to one definitional choice (gap/X handling, ortholog population, four-taxon filter)
DeepSeek-codex counted splice-region variants as coding (copied from a ToolUniverse script); a wide range lets three wrong cohorts pass
The accepted PC1 value depends on an unstated sample-exclusion rule that the harness's PCA skill imposes
Galaxy misses come from failed PyDESeq2 custom tools and a fallback to R DESeq2; code misses come from memory workarounds
All failures are DeepSeek-Claude-Code runs that replaced the per-kingdom trees with other distance sources
9/49 comes from fitting DESeq2 on all 30 samples instead of the 3-vs-3 subset; 8/47 from an added background
Two runs counted the header line kept by Galaxy's Filter; one reported the rows kept instead of removed
Code misses come from counting gaps as states or changing the sample; one correct code run read other agents' answers online
All three misses (superseded CC harness only) shrink the test to a "shared-ortholog" subset
Both "100" answers come from runs that installed BUSCO 5.7.1 locally; "64" comes from a hand-rolled BUSCO substitute
Rejected runs counted gaps as a character state; one accepted value relies on a protein-alphabet bug
Counting gaps as a character state inflated the maximum from 29 to 35
Both code failures are data-alignment bugs: genes or cell lines paired out of order
"Upregulation" follows from a 30-sample model; the six-sample CBD-vs-DMSO fit gives downregulation
2118 vs 2106 is only DESeq2's independent-filtering alpha; the two 2100s come from PyDESeq2
The one miss did not flip the sign of the DepMap gene-effect scores; this is not a data mismatch
The one miss comes from a fragile multi-tool Galaxy text pipeline whose correlations have the wrong sign
Galaxy PhyKIT-metrics wrapper's non-verbose value is the variance, not the median
Galaxy silently ran the default "total tree length" metric instead of "evolutionary rate"; one run reported that value
The only failure had the correct value from Galaxy and ended its turn before writing it
Galaxy sklearn defaults (liblinear, L2, penalized intercept) gave −0.027; the agent's own unpenalized fit was ignored
A digits-only header filter silently dropped the W and Z chromosomes
The only miss is `10.0%` for a fraction of 0.1; the parser read the percent value as 10.0
20.5045 came from re-trimming the raw subsample instead of mapping the supplied trimmed reads
Hidden key is almost certainly "E"; all 24 paired runs made the same computation and read it as "feedback loop" (D)
Only two real in-container runs got 29,556; the Galaxy `.dat` filename silently turned off adapter trimming (13,636), and host OpenSSL changed the pseudoreplicate split (~28.9k)
The apparent T allele is a 5′ read-end artifact; 20/25 runs trusted naive pileup counts
Each wrong answer is a partial union of three accession routes (suffix-stripped ENCSR, direct GSM, ENCODE dbxref GSM)
Only an exact P-value match to the MultiSuSiE revision release works; one of the two correct Galaxy runs copied the answer from a public trace of an earlier agent run
Input is PDB 3J04, the "F" of Howarth's protein alphabet; T is a side-view reading
"Omentum" is the published atlas label; "Lung" is what the cell's expression says
only runs that tested the Tn5 9-bp stagger chose 4; others picked quality or cell-line outliers
EBV (the sample's own lymphoblastoid virus) outranks the spiked-in pig reads unless human reads are removed first
Two real contaminants; the spiked chimpanzee reads disappear with primate-free databases or human subtraction, leaving a minor real Mycoplasma signal
"malignant basal" means all LUSC basal cells (46% -> 40) in the key, but the paper's 8,016 "malignant basal" subset gives 17% -> 20
Same cCRE in every run; "pELS" and "Proximal enhancer" are two spellings of one class, from different v4 distributions
The gene list is a published MSigDB set (CUI_CDC2_LIF_RESPONSE_UP); runs that found it were right, and runs limited to Enrichr/C7 enrichment defaulted to LPS
Every wrong vector comes from one +9 artefact: ortholog gene models with 3 extra upstream codons (ATG GGC GAG, "MGE")
F answers came from averaging over guides, which hides EP3's single-guide effect
The three FASTQs are nested prefixes; `90` counts a file-construction artifact, not an exogenous signal
The 10/30/60 split depends on excluding about 90 low-purity "human" barcodes; lenient purity cutoffs or Alevin re-filtering give 20/30/50
The 50-sample answer misses Coriell `GM` cell-line IDs that should map to 1000G `NA` sample IDs
GC confounding: gained peaks are AT-rich, so without a GC-matched background AT-rich motifs beat KLF4
wrong answers were unverified guesses; the correct source is an exact matrix match to GSM3578982
Wrong answers are 1-bp end-coordinate slips in motif-window scorers; two correct "Galaxy" answers were computed locally
All five misses are Luna runs that scored bulk genome-wide fragment fractions instead of ChIP-enriched sites
Wrong runs used an interferon-only threshold and so labelled most COVID donors "healthy"
Every wrong answer came from Scrublet; the doublet only shows up in fragment-overlap (AMULET-style) counting, and two correct DeepSeek Galaxy runs first read the barcode in a public third-party trace
Galaxy misses came from a failed core_nt Kraken2 job and a fallback database that lacks cnidarians; the code miss came from a hand-picked mammalian panel
STAT1 answers took the largest mean effect from a 5-cell guide and ignored "robustly"
The file is Yengo 2022's Hispanic-ancestry height sumstats; wrong runs stopped at trait or ancestry similarity without an exact row match
All three misses carry correct genotypes in phased notation; two runs copied the format from a leaked trace of another agent
The GPT-5.5 misses fit their k-mer classifier on the same reads it then scored; cross-validated fits give 30
The repeated SP1 exon makes SP1–ZIC2 junctions run both ways, and split-read graph filters drop them
the two misses are the right hit written with an inclusive end coordinate
8870 is the reverse-complement-averaged prediction; the key uses the forward pass only
Both misses called a highly expressed gene from 1-read or multimapper-only "novel" junctions, without requiring a junction pair that forms an exon
Both misses used a different chromatin-state model; one also queried hg19 files with hg38 coordinates
LD-profile inference reached HIS in every Galaxy run; the two code misses are an admixture near-miss and a compacted run's unsupported guess
Both wrong answers put an anchor outside the stated sub-compartment; one was copied from a third-party trace, and one correct Galaxy run computed locally
Both H3K4me1 answers read weak, short MACS2 peaks as enhancer peaks and never tested heterochromatin features
Both misses changed the coding/splice input tracks; one Galaxy "correct" answer was read from another run's history
The single miss used base-level `bedtools subtract` instead of dropping whole overlapping intervals (off by 453 bp)
The one miss ran bedtools slop with strand-awareness turned off on a minus-strand TSS
Luna Galaxy r1 fitted a post-hoc filter to noisy StringTie/Cuffdiff output and never ranked genes by read-supported switches
The single miss is hand arithmetic that sized pre-convolution BatchNorm layers by output rather than input channels (+4,608)
the only miss is a correct answer with " kcal/mol" appended; three Galaxy runs folded locally
the single miss mistook the chr22 pericentromeric mappability gap for the deletion
The miss counted on `.raw` instead of `.X` after computing both, then went looking for the benchmark's answer
The one miss built a pure-Galaxy bedtools pipeline whose exon-to-region join ignored transcript identity (+6 bp on CDS and 3' UTR)
The `TT` answer came from a broken local Caduceus reimplementation whose predictions were near-uniform
The single miss had the right haplotypes but encoded them against its own assembly contig, not hg38 primitives
The miss counted bowtie2's random primary placement of heavily multimapping reads instead of resolving them with EM
0.58 comes from applying the notebook's 1-based indexing to a 0-based table; 348/500 reference alleles were silently overwritten
Sol Galaxy r3 had the GEO source files but checked only file sizes and weak markers, which cannot see a same-size gut swap
The one miss relied on hand-made human-ortholog marker panels; correct runs used the published atlas
After UDTs failed, Sol Galaxy r2 used squidpy neighbourhood enrichment, which measures adjacency and misses Fibroblast_Stroma's distance-scale proximity
score plateaus follow the unstated truncation lengths; the two zeros come from lowercase staging slugs
score clusters track how strict PepQuery's competitive filtering was; the exact matches copied unstated workflow settings
all five "failures" are route-registry artifacts; every run removed host reads correctly
the three zeros are nuclear contigs picked without an identity check; the "0.9955 public record" cluster is a second valid MitoHiFi output
the 0.0 is a hard gate on a wrong BH step over otherwise-correct results; the 0.948 is an unshrunk NB GLM with no power
high scores come from per-route references, some built from the agents' own runs; the lowest run is penalized for summit splitting
Near-perfect scores hide changed significant-gene sets: PyDESeq2 loses YER164W, and Galaxy edgeR calls about 3× more genes

task_case_categories.C1: Equivalent answer expressed differently (label, genotype notation, interval convention, unit, identifier case)
task_case_categories.C2: Scoring or evaluator artifact (correct answer rejected, inconsistent rules, wrong route reference)
task_case_categories.C3: Reference depends on an unstated choice (definition, software version, sample set, threshold)
task_case_categories.C4: Galaxy platform, wrapper or server behaviour was the primary cause
task_case_categories.C5: Agent analysis error (method, statistics, domain knowledge, identifiers, unverified result)
task_case_categories.C6: Execution provenance or answer exposure is the main interpretive issue
task_case_categories.C7: Aggregate score conceals a changed scientific conclusion
